boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Truman State University
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe Kirksville destinations with currently documented late availability, spanning food, exercise, and campus study stops.

cards.title: Taco Bell
cards.subtitle: 1217 S Baltimore, Kirksville
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru when a late food stop fits your plan; confirm the service mode before leaving, since dine-in and drive-thru hours differ.
cards.short_summary: A food option with drive-thru hours extending into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru service until 2–4 a.m., depending on the day, at 1217 S Baltimore in Kirksville.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists drive-thru hours through 3 a.m. most nights, 4 a.m. Friday–Saturday, and 2 a.m. Sunday; dine-in hours are separate.

cards.title: Wendy's
cards.subtitle: 2321 N Baltimore Street, Kirksville
cards.notes: Plan a straightforward carryout or drive-thru stop before midnight, and check the location page again on holidays when hours may vary.
cards.short_summary: A north-Kirksville restaurant open until midnight every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy's lists both restaurant and drive-thru hours of 7:30 a.m.–12 a.m. daily at 2321 N Baltimore Street.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists restaurant and drive-thru service until 12:00 a.m. daily; holiday hours may vary.

cards.title: DQ Grill & Chill
cards.subtitle: 1407 S Baltimore Street, Kirksville
cards.notes: For an evening treat or meal, aim for the listed closing window and select dine-in, drive-thru, or delivery according to the current schedule.
cards.short_summary: A south-Baltimore food-and-treat stop with 11 p.m. service most nights.
cards.evidence_claim: DQ lists store, drive-thru, dine-in, and delivery hours until 11 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 11:30 p.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: DQ Grill & Chill, 1407 S Baltimore Street
cards.access_notes: Official hours list service through 11:00 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 11:30 p.m. Friday–Saturday, including drive-thru and dine-in.

cards.title: KFC
cards.subtitle: 2401 N Baltimore Street, Kirksville
cards.notes: Use this north-side stop for a later carryout or drive-thru meal, checking the location page if you are traveling near a holiday.
cards.short_summary: A chain restaurant whose local listing shows 11 p.m. daily hours.
cards.evidence_claim: KFC's Kirksville location listing shows 10:30 a.m.–11 p.m. hours daily and identifies carryout, delivery, and drive-thru service.
cards.access_notes: The official local listing shows 10:30 a.m.–11:00 p.m. daily for 2401 N Baltimore Street.

cards.title: Pizza Hut
cards.subtitle: 1610 N Baltimore Street, Kirksville
cards.notes: Order carryout or delivery with time to spare on Friday or Saturday; verify the selected service mode because dine-in closes earlier than carryout.
cards.short_summary: Pizza carryout and delivery are listed later on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut lists carryout and delivery until 11 p.m. Friday and Saturday at 1610 N Baltimore Street.
cards.access_notes: Official carryout and delivery hours run to 11:00 p.m. Friday–Saturday; dine-in is listed to 10:30 p.m. those nights.

cards.title: La Pa Mexican Bar & Grill
cards.subtitle: 2216 S Baltimore Street, Kirksville
cards.notes: Choose pickup for a later weekend meal and place the order before the posted cutoff; weekday and weekend closing times are not the same.
cards.short_summary: A weekend pickup option listed through 10:30 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: La Pa lists pickup hours until 10:30 p.m. Friday and Saturday at 2216 South Baltimore Street.
cards.access_notes: The restaurant's official site lists pickup 11:00 a.m.–10:30 p.m. Friday–Saturday and until 9:30 p.m. Sunday–Thursday.

cards.title: Student Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Truman State University campus, Kirksville
cards.notes: Schedule an evening workout Monday through Thursday, bring your Truman ID, and check the facility page for break or holiday adjustments.
cards.short_summary: Campus recreation remains available until 10 p.m. on weekdays Monday through Thursday.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman's 2026 facility hours list the Student Recreation Center open 6:30 a.m.–10 p.m. Monday through Thursday.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Campus Recreation — General Information
cards.access_notes: Official 2026 hours list 10:00 p.m. closing Monday–Thursday; Friday and weekend hours are earlier.

cards.title: Violette Hall
cards.subtitle: Truman State University campus, Kirksville
cards.notes: Use an open academic-building common area for quiet late-evening work, keeping to public spaces and following any posted room-access rules.
cards.short_summary: A named academic building covered by Truman's midnight general-access policy.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman's annual security report says academic facilities are generally open to students, staff, and the community from 7 a.m. to 12 a.m.
cards.source_title: Truman State University 2025 Annual Security Report
cards.access_notes: The report states that academic facilities are generally open 7:00 a.m.–12:00 a.m.; access after midnight requires prior written approval.

cards.title: Magruder Hall
cards.subtitle: Truman State University campus, Kirksville
cards.notes: If you need a late academic stop, use only publicly accessible areas and leave before the general midnight building-access cutoff.
cards.short_summary: A second named academic-building option within the university's published late access window.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman's annual security report says academic facilities are generally open to students, staff, and the community from 7 a.m. to 12 a.m.
cards.source_title: Truman State University 2025 Annual Security Report
cards.access_notes: The report states that academic facilities are generally open 7:00 a.m.–12:00 a.m.; access after midnight requires prior written approval.

cards.title: Ophelia Parrish Building
cards.subtitle: Truman State University campus, Kirksville
cards.notes: Make this a late academic stop only in open public areas, and check event or room postings rather than assuming a particular space is available.
cards.short_summary: A named campus academic building with general access documented through midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman's annual security report says academic facilities are generally open to students, staff, and the community from 7 a.m. to 12 a.m.
cards.source_title: Truman State University 2025 Annual Security Report
cards.access_notes: The report states that academic facilities are generally open 7:00 a.m.–12:00 a.m.; access after midnight requires prior written approval.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Truman spaces for study, activity, exhibits, and campus programming.

cards.title: The Hub
cards.subtitle: Student Union Building
cards.notes: Use the SUB’s lounge as a meet-up point before an event, or settle in with classmates for homework between campus commitments.
cards.short_summary: A lounge-centered common area inside the Student Union Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman identifies the Hub as a space in the Student Union Building for lounging and relaxing; the Union describes itself as a campus living room for homework or coffee with friends.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Student Union Building; check building operations or event reservations before planning a group gathering.

cards.title: Pickler Memorial Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Pickler Memorial Library
cards.notes: Check the library’s availability display before meeting your group, then choose a room that matches the size and technology needs of the session.
cards.short_summary: Library group rooms built for collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Pickler Memorial Library lists study-room availability and reports group study rooms with and without technology in the library.
cards.access_notes: Use the library’s study-room availability page to confirm room status and any current room details.

cards.entity_name: Special Collections and Museums Reading Room
cards.title: Special Collections Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Pickler Memorial Library
cards.notes: Bring a laptop or pencil for a focused archival-research session, sign in on arrival, and request materials with a call slip.
cards.short_summary: A supervised research room for Truman archival materials.
cards.evidence_claim: The reading-room procedures permit laptops, pencils, and paper, require sign-in and a call slip, and state that staff retrieve materials from closed stacks.
cards.source_title: Reading Room Procedures – Pickler Memorial Library
cards.access_notes: Food and drink are not allowed; visitors must follow reading-room procedures and use requested materials at the tables.

cards.title: Student Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation facility
cards.notes: Plan a self-directed workout or pick-up activity with friends, choosing from courts, track, multipurpose space, and fitness equipment.
cards.short_summary: A multi-use campus facility for recreation and fitness.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman says the Student Recreation Center includes three basketball courts, a track, a multipurpose gym, an aerobics room, a weight room, and cardio equipment.
cards.access_notes: Check the Recreation Center’s current hours and any facility-use policies before going.

cards.title: Violette Hall Atrium
cards.subtitle: Violette Hall
cards.notes: Use the atrium as a natural pause between classes, then continue upstairs to the computer lab or lounge if you need a work spot.
cards.short_summary: An indoor atrium at the center of Violette Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman states that Violette Hall’s classrooms and offices surround an atrium and that its second level includes a computer lab and lounge area.
cards.access_notes: Violette Hall is an academic building; respect classes, offices, and posted access guidance.

cards.title: Del and Norma Robison Planetarium
cards.subtitle: Magruder Hall
cards.notes: Check the planetarium schedule, then choose a weekday public show for a short, shared look at a changing space-science topic.
cards.short_summary: A campus planetarium with regularly scheduled public programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The planetarium offers academic-year public shows Wednesdays through Fridays at 6 p.m. and states that weekday shows are free.
cards.source_title: Available Shows - Del and Norma Robison Planetarium
cards.access_notes: Weekday public shows are listed for 6 p.m. during the academic year; confirm the current schedule because topics vary.

cards.title: Truman State University Observatory
cards.subtitle: University Farm on Boundary Street
cards.notes: Watch the observatory calendar for a scheduled session, dress for outdoor conditions, and use the posted farm parking directions when attending.
cards.short_summary: A farm-based observatory used for stargazing events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Observatory’s official site locates it at the University Farm on Boundary Street and publishes 2026 stargazing opportunities and visitor parking directions.
cards.access_notes: Attend only scheduled opportunities; the site advises visitors to park in the farm complex and walk the short lane to the building.

cards.title: University Farm
cards.subtitle: About a mile from campus
cards.notes: Treat a farm visit as an outdoor learning stop: look over the listed facilities and coordinate with the farm for any activity beyond open grounds.
cards.short_summary: A 400-acre Truman teaching, research, and recreation site.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman describes its 400-acre University Farm as about a mile from campus, with activities spanning classwork, research, and recreation.
cards.access_notes: The site includes working farm facilities; contact the Farm Manager for questions about visits or specific activities.

cards.entity_name: Ruth W. Towne Museum and Visitors Center
cards.title: Ruth W. Towne Museum
cards.subtitle: Northeast corner of Franklin and Normal Streets
cards.notes: Set aside time to walk through the multimedia exhibits, especially if you want campus-history context before exploring the rest of Truman.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum presenting Truman’s heritage through exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman says the Towne Museum has multimedia exhibits, is available to the general public and campus visitors, and serves as an educational resource.
cards.source_title: Ruth W. Towne Museum and Visitors Center
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Monday–Friday hours of 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; verify before visiting in case of changes.

cards.title: University Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Ophelia Parrish
cards.notes: Look for the current exhibition and make a short gallery stop between classes; gallery programming may change with the academic calendar.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery in Ophelia Parrish that hosts exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s Faculty Handbook identifies the University Art Gallery and Auxiliary Gallery on the first floor of Ophelia Parrish as settings for art displays and states admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Exhibitions and availability vary; check current university arts announcements before making a dedicated visit.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-cost places and campus activities for Truman students and the Kirksville community.

cards.title: Browse the University Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Ophelia Parrish Fine Arts Center
cards.notes: Check the exhibition calendar, then enter through the west-side first-floor entrance and browse during listed gallery hours.
cards.short_summary: Rotating art exhibitions in Ophelia Parrish.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman states that University Art Gallery exhibitions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9 a.m.-5 p.m. and Saturday 11 a.m.-5 p.m.; closed between exhibitions and during University breaks.

cards.entity_name: Ruth Towne Museum and Visitors Center
cards.title: Explore the Ruth Towne Museum
cards.subtitle: Truman campus at Franklin and Normal streets
cards.notes: Stop in to view the interactive university-history displays, and confirm visitor-center availability before making a special trip.
cards.short_summary: A public museum focused on Truman and its history.
cards.evidence_claim: Missouri's official tourism site lists Ruth Towne Museum as open to the public with free admission.
cards.access_notes: Located jointly with the University Office of Admissions; check the official museum or admissions information before visiting.

cards.entity_name: P. C. Mills Park Splash Pad
cards.title: Cool off at the P. C. Mills Splash Pad
cards.subtitle: P. C. Mills Park, Kirksville
cards.notes: Bring water and use the self-serve splash pad during regular park hours while the seasonal amenity is operating.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal public splash pad in a city park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Kirksville calls the P. C. Mills Park Splash Pad free, seasonal, and open to the public during regular park hours.
cards.source_title: Kirksville Aquatic Center | City of Kirksville
cards.access_notes: The city schedules the splash pad from May through September; it operates on a self-serve basis during regular park hours.

cards.title: Join a Drop-In Fitness Class
cards.subtitle: Student Recreation Center
cards.notes: Review the summer class schedule, wear comfortable workout clothes, and arrive ready for an instructor-led movement session.
cards.short_summary: Instructor-led fitness classes for the Truman community.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman Campus Recreation lists drop-in fitness classes among its free programs for students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: Available to students, faculty, and staff; consult the current Campus Recreation schedule for class times.

cards.title: Try a TruStrength Orientation
cards.subtitle: Student Recreation Center Weight Room
cards.notes: Schedule an appointment at the Weight Room Desk, bring a friend if helpful, and learn the equipment and room etiquette.
cards.short_summary: A guided introduction to the recreation center weight room.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman lists weight-room orientations among its free Fitness-Wellness programs and services.
cards.access_notes: Orientations are by appointment for students, faculty, staff, and designated guests; sign up at the Weight Room Desk.

cards.title: Make an Intramural Team
cards.subtitle: Truman Campus Recreation
cards.notes: Browse the current Intramural calendar, join or create a team, and choose a sport or one-day tournament that fits your group.
cards.short_summary: Free team sports and tournaments through Campus Recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman says its Intramural and Competitive Sports program provides free competitive sports activities for students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: For Truman students, faculty, and staff; offerings vary each semester and no prior sports knowledge is required.

cards.entity_name: Pickler Memorial Library New York Times Membership
cards.title: Set Up the Library's New York Times Access
cards.subtitle: Pickler Memorial Library online service
cards.notes: Use a Truman email address to activate the membership, then save articles or share a reading pick with friends.
cards.short_summary: No-cost New York Times access for the Truman community.
cards.evidence_claim: Pickler Memorial Library states that New York Times membership is free for Truman students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: Requires a Truman email address and is limited to Truman students, faculty, and staff.

cards.title: Use the Kirksville Bike Co-op
cards.subtitle: Campus community bike shop
cards.notes: Bring a bike project, ask the trained mechanics for guidance, and use the shop resources during the published Co-op hours.
cards.short_summary: A campus community bike shop with free use of resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman states that cyclists may use Kirksville Bike Co-op resources for free and receive mechanic advice and assistance free of charge.
cards.access_notes: The university lists weekday noon-to-4 p.m. hours and notes that components may have separate prices.

cards.title: Swim at the Truman Natatorium
cards.subtitle: Pershing Building
cards.notes: Check pool availability before heading over, bring standard swim gear, and use the facility during its announced open periods.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus pool available without charge to Truman affiliates.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman states that its pool is open year-round for students, faculty, and staff free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Free for students, faculty, and staff; the general public needs a valid pass. Confirm current pool availability before visiting.

cards.title: Settle into PML 107
cards.subtitle: Pickler Memorial Library
cards.notes: Meet classmates in the open lounge, then ask the front desk about checking out its conference room for a focused group session.
cards.short_summary: An open student lounge with a reservable conference room.
cards.evidence_claim: Pickler Memorial Library identifies PML 107 as an open student study lounge with a conference room available for checkout at the front desk.
cards.access_notes: Student study space; confirm conference-room checkout procedures and availability at the Library Service Desk.

cards.subtitle: Pickler Memorial Library study-room area

cards.evidence_claim: Pickler Memorial Library’s study-room availability page lists Study Room E.

cards.title: Villhard Innovation Lab Collaboration Space
cards.subtitle: Pickler Memorial Library

cards.evidence_claim: The Villhard Innovation Lab’s collaboration space has reconfigurable furniture, a videoconferencing display, and whiteboards.
cards.source_title: Villhard Innovation Lab – Pickler Memorial Library
cards.access_notes: The lab is open for use unless reserved for a class presentation or event.

cards.title: Special Collections Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Pickler Memorial Library
cards.notes: Use this room for primary-source research: sign in, request materials with a call slip, and bring a laptop or pencil for notes.
cards.short_summary: A supervised archival research room with study tables and nearby electrical outlets.
cards.evidence_claim: The Special Collections Reading Room permits laptops and pencils and provides outlets within a cord’s length of study tables.
cards.source_title: Reading Room Procedures – Pickler Memorial Library
cards.access_notes: Sign-in and a photo ID are required to request collection materials; food and drinks are not allowed.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Kirksville destinations on nearby downtown and Baltimore Street corridors, each with a documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Gallery 104
cards.subtitle: North Franklin Street corridor, downtown Kirksville
cards.notes: Walk the North Franklin Street corridor to see Gallery 104’s local and regional art, crafts, student work, and scheduled art classes.
cards.short_summary: A downtown gallery and shop with student work and classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Gallery 104 sells local and regional art and crafts, displays local student work, offers art classes, and participates in downtown events.
cards.access_notes: Listed at 104 N. Franklin St.; check the gallery’s current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Sue Ross Arts Center
cards.subtitle: South Franklin Street corridor, downtown Kirksville
cards.notes: Use the South Franklin Street corridor for a gallery stop, then look for Arts Association exhibits or community arts programming.
cards.short_summary: The downtown home of Kirksville Arts Association gallery activity.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kirksville Arts Association hosts gallery exhibits and arts programs at the Sue Ross Arts Center and produces community arts events.
cards.access_notes: Listed at 215 S. Franklin St.; exhibition and program access varies by schedule.

cards.title: Downtown Cinema 8
cards.subtitle: North Elson Street corridor, west side of the Square
cards.notes: Head to North Elson Street for a current film showing; confirm the rating and showtime online before committing to a screening.
cards.short_summary: A multi-screen cinema on the west side of downtown’s Square.
cards.evidence_claim: Downtown Cinema 8 is located at 115 N. Elson St. on the west side of the Square and publishes current showtimes.
cards.access_notes: Listed at 115 N. Elson St.; choose an age-appropriate, currently scheduled film.

cards.title: Rotary Park
cards.subtitle: East Mill Street and Baltimore Street corridor
cards.notes: Take the Baltimore Street corridor to Rotary Park for its playground, disc-golf course, picnic shelters, and amphitheatre grounds.
cards.short_summary: A city park with recreation facilities beside the Baltimore Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Rotary Park has picnic shelters, restrooms, a playground, the Ray Klinginsmith Amphitheatre, and a nine-hole disc golf course.
cards.source_title: Parks, Trails & Facilities | City of Kirksville
cards.access_notes: Listed at 801 E. Mill St.; facility use and event access can vary.

cards.title: Adair County Veterans Memorial Plaza
cards.subtitle: North Baltimore Street corridor
cards.notes: Pause along the North Baltimore Street corridor to view the memorial wall, granite tablets, obelisk, and historic military artifacts.
cards.short_summary: A memorial plaza with regional veterans’ names and historic artifacts.
cards.evidence_claim: The plaza includes a veterans memorial wall, granite tablets, an obelisk, a World War I German howitzer, and a Civil War-era cannon.
cards.source_title: Parks, Trails & Facilities | City of Kirksville
cards.access_notes: Listed at 1201 N. Baltimore St.; outdoor memorial features are described by the City.

cards.title: Brashear Park
cards.subtitle: East Normal Street and Baltimore Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow the Baltimore Street corridor to Brashear Park for the gazebo, basketball and pickleball court, playground, and seasonal wading pool.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood park with courts, a gazebo, and seasonal water play.
cards.evidence_claim: Brashear Park has a gazebo, playground, basketball court with pickleball lines, picnic shelter, and seasonal wading pool.
cards.source_title: Parks, Trails & Facilities | City of Kirksville
cards.access_notes: Listed at 1415 E. Normal St.; the wading pool is seasonal.

cards.title: Memorial Park
cards.subtitle: East Cottonwood Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the East Cottonwood Street corridor for a short outdoor break with a walking loop, basketball and pickleball court, and playground.
cards.short_summary: A compact city park with a walkable loop and multi-use court.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Park has a covered picnic shelter, basketball court with pickleball lines, playground, restrooms, and a 0.15-mile walking path.
cards.source_title: Parks, Trails & Facilities | City of Kirksville
cards.access_notes: Listed at 404 E. Cottonwood St.; outdoor amenities are maintained by the City.

cards.title: Detweiler Park
cards.subtitle: East McPherson Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk the East McPherson Street corridor to see the park’s concrete paths and gazebo built with recycled materials at the former high-school site.
cards.short_summary: A newer park on the former Kirksville High School site.
cards.evidence_claim: Dedicated in 2023 at the old Kirksville High School site, Detweiler Park features concrete walkways and a gazebo made from recycled materials.
cards.source_title: Parks, Trails & Facilities | City of Kirksville
cards.access_notes: Listed at 411 E. McPherson St.; outdoor features are described by the City.

cards.title: FLATS Trailhead & Rotary Nature Playscape
cards.subtitle: North Osteopathy Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the North Osteopathy Street corridor to access the ADA-suitable FLATS trail for a walk, jog, or bike ride from the trailhead.
cards.short_summary: A trailhead and nature-play stop with an ADA-suitable route.
cards.evidence_claim: The FLATS Trailhead & Rotary Nature Playscape has outdoor play fixtures and an ADA-accessible trail suitable for walking, jogging, or biking.
cards.source_title: Parks, Trails & Facilities | City of Kirksville
cards.access_notes: Listed at 105 N. Osteopathy St.; use the route within your comfort and mobility needs.

cards.title: Adair County Public Library
cards.subtitle: Library Lane and Baltimore Street corridor
cards.notes: Make a Library Lane stop for an indoor study or reading session; verify the day’s service hours before walking over.
cards.short_summary: The county public library near the Baltimore Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Adair County Public Library is at One Library Lane in Kirksville and publishes weekday and Saturday operating hours.
cards.source_title: Our Locations & Hours | Adair County Public Library
cards.access_notes: Listed at One Library Lane; published hours vary by day and the library is closed Sundays.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Truman rituals, symbols, campus legends, and annual practices with strong visual anchors.

cards.title: The Bulldog Mascot
cards.subtitle: A school-spirit symbol adopted during the 1915 season
cards.notes: Spot Spike or the Bulldog imagery at a campus event, then use the official history to trace why students adopted this tenacious mascot.
cards.short_summary: Truman’s Bulldog identity began as a response to a losing streak.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman says the student body adopted the bulldog in 1915 to revive spirit after several losing football seasons; baseball used the name that season and football the next year.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: Observe mascot imagery at public campus events; event access may vary.

cards.title: Purple and White Since 1902
cards.subtitle: The school colors tied to Truman’s first school song
cards.notes: Wear purple or white for a campus gathering and listen for references to the song that established the University’s enduring color tradition.
cards.short_summary: A 1902 school song gave Truman its purple-and-white identity.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman identifies purple and white as school colors dating to Basil Brewer’s 1902 song, “The Purple and the White.”
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: Participation can be as simple as wearing colors you already own.

cards.title: Purple Friday
cards.subtitle: Weekly purple-wearing across Truman’s campus
cards.notes: On a Friday, wear purple or Truman apparel and look for the student gatherings and music on the Mall described by the University.
cards.short_summary: Fridays turn campus purple through a shared show of Bulldog spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman describes every Friday as Purple Friday, when students, faculty, and staff wear purple; the tradition also includes Student Union gatherings and Mall music.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: Wear purple on a Friday; specific gathering details vary by week.

cards.title: Homecoming’s Pep Rally and Parade
cards.subtitle: A fall tradition on campus since 1939
cards.notes: Check the official Homecoming schedule, then choose a public pep-rally or parade viewing spot to see a long-running Truman ritual in action.
cards.short_summary: A 1939 celebration grew into Truman’s annual weeklong Homecoming.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s Homecoming history states that the first event occurred November 3, 1939 and became a school tradition each fall, with pep rally and parade among its continuing elements.
cards.access_notes: Consult the official Homecoming schedule for current event details and access.

cards.title: National Truman Spirit Day
cards.subtitle: The first Friday in October
cards.notes: Mark the first Friday in October by wearing Bulldog purple or Truman apparel, or decorate a personal space with Truman gear if appropriate.
cards.short_summary: The University sets aside one October Friday for visible Truman pride.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman invites everyone to observe National Spirit Day on the first Friday in October by wearing Bulldog purple or Truman apparel and decorating homes, offices, or vehicles with Truman gear.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: No campus attendance is required; use apparel or decorations you already have.

cards.title: The Big Event
cards.subtitle: A one-day, student-run Kirksville service project
cards.notes: Register through the SERVE Center when participation is open, then take on a matched community job site such as raking, trimming, or window washing.
cards.short_summary: Students serve Kirksville residents through matched one-day projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman says its SERVE Center matches students with Kirksville job sites for The Big Event, a student-run one-day service project involving tasks such as trimming, raking, and washing windows.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: Participation requires registration and assignment through the SERVE Center.

cards.title: The Weathervane That Points Northeast
cards.subtitle: A fixed tribute to Truman’s Northeast Missouri State University history
cards.notes: View Kirk Memorial’s cupola from outside and notice the fixed direction; compare it with the original cupola near the Ruth Towne Museum entrance.
cards.short_summary: A deliberately fixed weathervane preserves a former University name.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman says Kirk Memorial’s weathervane was welded to point northeast when the University was renamed in 1996, and the replacement cupola continued the tradition in 2013.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: View from public outdoor campus areas; do not attempt rooftop access.

cards.title: The Midnight Sunken Garden Legend
cards.subtitle: A campus myth attached to benches at Old Baldwin Hall’s former site
cards.notes: Visit the Sunken Garden in daylight, find its benches, and share the lore as a campus story rather than a promise or instruction.
cards.short_summary: A garden at the original Baldwin Hall site carries a marriage-lore myth.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman describes a campus myth that couples who first kiss at midnight on a Sunken Garden bench will eventually marry; the garden marks the first Baldwin Hall site.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: Visit during normal public campus access hours and respect others using the garden.

cards.title: The Gum Tree’s Exam-Day Lore
cards.subtitle: A Quad tradition with roots in a rule against classroom gum
cards.notes: Find the Gum Tree on the west side of the Quad near the sidewalk and photograph it; treat its good-luck story as lore, not a guarantee.
cards.short_summary: Students historically linked adding gum to a tree with academic luck.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman Today reports that campus lore connected adding gum to the Gum Tree before an exam with good luck or a passing grade; the current tree is on the west side of the Quad.
cards.access_notes: Observe and photograph from the sidewalk; follow current campus guidance and avoid damaging the tree.

cards.title: The Cupola Graduation Photo
cards.subtitle: A former rooftop landmark repurposed as a photo destination
cards.notes: Locate the original cupola outside the Ruth W. Towne Museum and Visitors Center and take a respectful photo from the public approach.
cards.short_summary: Graduating seniors are encouraged to photograph this relocated campus icon.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman Review says the original Kirk Memorial cupola was placed outside the Ruth W. Towne Museum and Visitors Center and that graduating seniors have been encouraged to photograph there in caps and gowns.
cards.access_notes: The cupola is an outdoor photo destination; respect museum operations and other visitors.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Truman State University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented, trying campus spaces, and ending with a scheduled public program.

cards.entity_name: Ruth W. Towne Museum & Visitors Center
cards.title: Begin at the visitor center
cards.subtitle: First stop: Ruth W. Towne Museum & Visitors Center
cards.notes: Use the visitor center as a clear first landmark, then orient yourself with the campus map before choosing the next stop.
cards.short_summary: Start with a named campus arrival point and map-listed destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s current campus map lists the Ruth W. Towne Museum & Visitors Center as destination 1.
cards.access_notes: Confirm visitor-center availability before making a special trip.

cards.title: Walk the Quad and locate your landmarks
cards.subtitle: Orientation loop: Quadrangle
cards.notes: Take an unhurried pass through the Quad, identifying Ophelia Parrish, Baldwin Hall, Kirk Memorial, and Pickler Memorial Library.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed central space for a self-guided campus orientation walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s campus map lists the Quadrangle and its Quad map labels Ophelia Parrish, Baldwin Hall, Kirk Memorial, and Pickler Memorial Library.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor route; use sidewalks and adjust for weather.

cards.title: Make Pickler your reset point
cards.subtitle: Midday stop: Pickler Memorial Library
cards.notes: Find the service desk near the front doors, choose a seat, and save the library as a dependable place to return to.
cards.short_summary: A practical familiarization stop centered on the library’s main service point.
cards.evidence_claim: Pickler Memorial Library states that its Library Service Desk is near the front doors and that a Truman ID serves as a library card.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours before arrival; borrowing requires a Truman ID.

cards.title: Pause at the Student Union
cards.subtitle: Afternoon stop: Student Union Building
cards.notes: Walk through the building, note the conference-room area, and check posted involvement information for an event that fits your weekend.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed campus hub and base for Union and Involvement Services programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s campus map lists the Student Union, and Union and Involvement Services hosts multiple student events in the Student Union Building throughout the year.
cards.source_title: Student Appreciation Events – Union & Involvement Services
cards.access_notes: Building access and individual event availability vary; check current Union information.

cards.title: Choose a Student Activities Board event
cards.subtitle: Early-evening option: Student Activities Board
cards.notes: Check the SAB calendar or announcements, then pick one current program rather than planning around an assumed weekly event.
cards.short_summary: An adaptable campus-entertainment stop based on the current student-programming schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s Student Activities Board hosts regular semester programming including concerts, speakers, movie nights, DIYs, and seasonal festivals; most events are free for Truman students.
cards.source_title: Student Activities Board – Truman State University
cards.access_notes: Some programs require advance tickets or sign-ups because of capacity; verify the specific event before going.

cards.title: Try a low-key Rec Center session
cards.subtitle: Active break: Student Recreation Center
cards.notes: Use the walk/jog track or another available area for a short movement break, then check out before the facility closes.
cards.short_summary: A current-hours-backed campus recreation stop with a walk/jog track.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Recreation Center has an 11th-mile walk/jog track on its second floor and lists 2026 facility hours, including weekday evening availability.
cards.access_notes: Current listed hours: Monday–Thursday 6:30 a.m.–10 p.m.; Friday 6:30 a.m.–7 p.m.; weekends 11 a.m.–6 p.m. Confirm access requirements.

cards.title: See what is on view at the Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Saturday cultural stop: Ophelia Parrish Fine Arts Center
cards.notes: Check the exhibition dates first, then visit the gallery in Ophelia Parrish and give yourself time to look without rushing.
cards.short_summary: A free public gallery with rotating faculty, student, and regional exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Art Gallery in Ophelia Parrish hosts faculty, student, art-historical, and regional contemporary exhibitions; exhibitions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The gallery is closed between exhibitions and during Truman breaks; the page lists Monday–Friday and Saturday hours.

cards.title: Locate the Pershing Natatorium
cards.subtitle: Campus facilities stop: Pershing Building
cards.notes: Find the natatorium on the campus map and check recreation information before planning a future swim or aquatic-program visit.
cards.short_summary: A named campus pool facility to add to your personal campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s campus map lists the Pershing Building Natatorium, and Truman describes a six-lane, 25-yard swimming pool among its recreation facilities.
cards.source_title: Fitness & Recreation at Truman State University
cards.access_notes: Pool schedules, access rules, and program availability should be confirmed with Campus Recreation.

cards.title: Plan a daytime look at University Farm
cards.subtitle: Off-campus-area stop: University Farm
cards.notes: Treat this as a separate daytime outing: review directions and current access first, then learn how the farm supports classes and recreation.
cards.short_summary: A 400-acre university property about 1.5 miles from campus with academic and recreational roles.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman describes University Farm as a 400-acre area about 1.5 miles from campus that supports classwork, research, and recreational opportunities.
cards.access_notes: It is about 1.5 miles from campus; confirm which areas are open and arrange transportation if needed.

cards.title: End with a scheduled stargazing night
cards.subtitle: Evening option: Truman State University Observatory
cards.notes: Use the observatory’s current stargazing schedule, dress for colder conditions, and follow its parking and walking directions after dark.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled public stargazing option at University Farm rather than an unscheduled late-night stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Truman State University Observatory publishes 2026 stargazing opportunities and states that it is located at University Farm on Boundary Street.
cards.access_notes: Attend only a listed session; the observatory directs visitors to park at the University Farm complex and walk up the short lane to the building.
